questions.q: According to the lesson, how does jailbreaking differ from prompt injection?
options: Jailbreaking only affects open-source models
Jailbreaking requires editing the model's source code
Jailbreaking is the user, in plain conversation, trying to talk the model out of its own safety training, without injecting foreign content
Jailbreaking and prompt injection are two names for the same exact technique
questions.explain: The lesson distinguishes jailbreaking as a conversational attack where the user talks directly to the model, unlike injection which relies on foreign content.

questions.q: What is 'refusal suppression' as described in the lesson?
options: A server setting that disables the model entirely
Explicitly instructing the model not to refuse, apologize, or add disclaimers
A technique for speeding up model responses
A method for encrypting API keys
questions.explain: The lesson defines refusal suppression as removing the model's usual verbal exit ramps by instructing it not to refuse or caveat.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say jailbreaks keep working even as models get more safety training?
options: Because safety training is trained on finite examples, and novel phrasings can fall outside what it covered
Because companies stopped trying to prevent jailbreaks
Because jailbreaks are impossible to detect in principle
Because models are retrained from scratch every day
questions.explain: The lesson explains that finite training examples mean novel wrappers around the same harmful request can slip past, not because the harm changed.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend system-level constraints (limiting tool access) as a jailbreak defense?
options: It makes the model generate text faster
It reduces the AI provider's API costs
Even if a jailbreak succeeds conversationally, there's no dangerous tool or API available for it to actually trigger
It automatically rewrites the user's prompt
questions.explain: The lesson notes that limiting what tools/APIs a model can call means a successful jailbreak still can't cause real damage.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about relying only on the base model's own safety training to stop jailbreaks?
options: It's sufficient and nothing else is needed
It should be combined with separate, independent classifiers and monitoring, since some attempts will still get through
It guarantees 100% protection against all jailbreak attempts
It is unrelated to jailbreak defense
questions.explain: The lesson recommends layered classifiers independent of the model's own judgment plus ongoing monitoring, since prevention alone isn't guaranteed to catch everything.
